title: Indonesia’s aircraft carrier is an indulgence, not a strategy
gist: Indonesia will commission the donated 40-year-old Italian carrier Garibaldi at Ratai Bay on 20 September 2026, but refurbishment is estimated at $400–936 million plus roughly $5.5 million a month to operate — spending the author argues is prestige-driven and displaces the frigates and destroyers an archipelagic navy actually needs. The deeper problem is that Indonesia has had no defence white paper since 2015, leaving force structure untethered from strategy and arms transfers unaligned with Jakarta's goals.

insights.claim: Indonesia will commission the former Italian aircraft carrier Garibaldi on 20 September 2026, basing it at Ratai Bay in Lampung after receiving it from Italy as a grant donation.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: A hard date and basing location for a first-ever Indonesian carrier — watch Lampung port infrastructure, refit yards and aviation-support contracts for the follow-on spend.
insights.quote: On September 20, Indonesia will welcome (Opens in new window) the former Italian aircraft carrier Garibaldi into its fleet, basing it at Ratai Bay in Lampung.

insights.claim: Italy gave the Garibaldi away because scrapping the ship would have cost more than donating it — the "free" transfer is a disposal decision, not a strategic gift.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Frames the deal's true economics: the donor's incentive was cost avoidance, so the recipient absorbs all lifecycle cost — a pattern to expect in other second-hand naval transfers.
insights.quote: Scrapping the ship would have cost Italy more than giving it away.
insights.locator: Decommissioned by the Italian Navy in 2024

insights.claim: Indonesian MP Tubagus Hasanuddin of the parliamentary defence commission puts the Garibaldi refurbishment bill at Rp7.2–16.8 trillion ($400–936 million) depending on specifications, with roughly a decade of service life remaining on a 40-year-old hull.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: A near-$1bn refit envelope on a ten-year asset sets a concrete addressable market for shipyard, propulsion and combat-systems vendors — and a concrete opportunity cost for Indonesia's frigate programs.
insights.quote: puts (Opens in new window) the refurbishment bill at Rp7.2 trillion to Rp16.8 trillion ($400–936 million) depending on specifications
insights.locator: Tubagus Hasanuddin, a member of parliament’s defence commission

insights.claim: Recurring carrier operating costs — estimated at roughly Rp101 billion (about $5.5 million) per month, or around $66 million a year — sit entirely outside the quoted refurbishment figure.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Recurring opex, not the acquisition price, is where donated platforms break defence budgets — the metric to track when assessing Indonesia's procurement headroom for other programs.
insights.quote: which he estimates to be roughly Rp101 billion (about $5.5 million) a month
insights.locator: None of which counts the recurring cost

insights.claim: The Indonesian Ministry of Defence targeted delivery of the carrier before 5 October, the TNI's 81st anniversary, indicating the acquisition timetable was set by symbolism rather than capability need.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Ceremonial deadlines compress refit and crew-training schedules — a leading indicator of cost overruns and low availability rates on the delivered platform.
insights.quote: the Ministry of Defence was targeting a delivery before 5 October, the date of the Indonesian National Armed Forces’ (TNI) 81st Anniversary

insights.claim: Indonesia is buying the symbol of a capability before writing the doctrine to use it, inverting the sequence in which a navy builds surface-fleet competence first and adds a carrier once it can integrate one.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: A reusable test for emerging-market defence programs: prestige platforms bought ahead of institutional capacity signal weak execution risk-adjusted returns for suppliers and slow follow-on orders.
insights.quote: rather than buying the symbol first and inventing the doctrine later
insights.locator: Building that fleet, and the institutional knowledge

insights.claim: The same Indonesian politicians who approved the Garibaldi transfer had themselves raised concerns about funding, operating costs and required doctrinal adjustments — approval came despite, not because of, resolved objections.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Parliamentary reservations that survive approval are a marker of later budget fights — watch for supplementary appropriations or a stalled refit.
insights.quote: Tellingly, the same politicians who approved the transfer raised exactly those worries surrounding funding, operating costs, and the doctrinal adjustments that the ship will demand.
insights.locator: Tellingly, the same politicians who approved

insights.claim: Indonesia's archipelagic geography gives it a maritime domain of nearly two million square miles to police, a patrol, sovereignty-enforcement and disaster-response mission set that carriers cannot cover efficiently.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Sizes the real requirement — distributed hulls and presence, which points demand toward corvettes, frigates and patrol vessels rather than capital ships.
insights.quote: having an archipelagic geography that hands it a maritime domain of nearly two million square miles to police
insights.locator: That is doubly true for Indonesia

insights.claim: Workhorse frigates and destroyers would give Indonesia multi-mission maritime coverage at far lower cost, and building that fleet plus the institutional knowledge to run it is the precondition for ever operating a carrier effectively.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Points the durable Indonesian naval budget toward surface-combatant primes rather than carrier-adjacent systems — the more investable line of demand.
insights.quote: Workhorse frigates and destroyers provide that avenue at a far more affordable cost.

insights.claim: The "kapal induk" or mother-ship reframe — judging the Garibaldi as a mobile hub for helicopters, drones and sea-basing rather than a strike platform — fails because a ship built to fly Harrier jump jets carries strike-carrier cost for a role a purpose-built amphibious or aviation-support vessel fills for far less.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: If Jakarta later concedes the point, demand shifts to LHD/LPD-class amphibious hulls — a different set of shipbuilders than carrier refit specialists.
insights.quote: built to fly fixed-wing Harrier jump jets, it carries the cost and heritage of a strike carrier for a role a purpose-built amphibious or aviation-support ship fills for far less
insights.locator: If the mission is a floating aviation-and-command node

insights.claim: Under Prabowo Subianto, first as defence minister and now as President, Indonesia is ordering or courting fighters from France, Türkiye, South Korea and China while also flirting with Russian jets, producing a menagerie of incompatible systems.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Multi-vendor fragmentation means no single prime locks the Indonesian air fleet, but it raises sustainment and integration spend — favourable for MRO and systems-integration providers, negative for platform economics.
insights.quote: It is ordering or courting fighters from France (Opens in new window), Türkiye (Opens in new window), South Korea (Opens in new window), and China (Opens in new window) – while also flirting with Russian (Opens in new window) jets.
insights.locator: Under Prabowo Subianto’s tenure as defence minister

insights.claim: Indonesia's supplier-diversification instinct traces to the 1990s, when Washington grounded Indonesia's F-16s and Western embargoes over East Timor left the TNI badly weakened — an embargo-avoidance reflex, not an efficiency choice.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Explains why Jakarta will keep spreading orders across blocs regardless of interoperability costs — Western exporters should not expect exclusivity from Indonesia.
insights.quote: This menagerie of incompatible systems stems from the anxiety of the 1990s, when Washington grounded Indonesia’s F-16s, and Western embargoes over East Timor left the TNI badly weakened.

insights.claim: Indonesia has not published a defence white paper since 2015, leaving its own institutions without a shared blueprint linking force structure to strategy and leaving partners unable to align cooperation and arms transfers with Jakarta's goals.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: A new Indonesian defence white paper would be the single highest-signal catalyst for reading Jakarta's procurement direction — its absence is why current orders look random.
insights.quote: Indonesia has not published a defence white paper (Opens in new window) since 2015.
insights.locator: What this really points to is the need for strategic clarity

insights.claim: Absent a fresh strategy document, prestige will keep driving Indonesian defence decisions — the author's forward prediction, exemplified by a carrier the country neither needs nor can properly crew.
insights.speaker: Awais Feroze Hanif
insights.so_what: Expect further symbolic big-ticket acquisitions from Jakarta rather than coherent fleet-building until a white paper lands — plan bids and forecasts accordingly.
insights.quote: Without a fresh strategy, prestige will keep driving Indonesia's defence decisions – starting with a carrier it neither needs nor can properly crew.
